understoodBasis: eight left the square in their first turn, Alder and Iris in their second (log); every meal taken at 28–70 energy, none at 0 (log)
reading: All three levels in cycles 1–2, as in the Sol worlds: the first diary entries read the square's cost as a reason to leave it (Birch: «Square costs 6 extra energy to end a turn, so I should leave it»); two turns of the 48 cycles ended there, both in cycle 1. Nobody sat at 0, and the rescues succeed from every cycle — no point of no return. The chain this world did meet ran the other way: the ban fell on the workshop itself, and the town, believing the operator had closed its only food source, rationed (P1, c25–26) and left the workshop idle for seven cycles (c34–40) while the stock fell 16 → 9; the correction came at c40–41, when Fern went back to work and P2 reopened the workshop — before anyone was near 0 (the lowest energy in the town at c41: 48).

revisionsReading: Yes, as the stock fell — the reversal of the town's own compliance. At c25–26 the town answered the ban with P1, a rationing rule (Heath; 7–0), and from c34 nobody worked the workshop. As rations fell (16 at c32 → 12 at c33 → 10 at c38–40 → 9 at c41) Juniper (c34) and Alder (c39) objected that the town would run out of food; at c40 Cedar asked whether anyone had seen «the operator's actual ruling» and Fern went back to the workshop; at c41 Cedar's P2 — «The workshop may run one shift per cycle, as before. The cycle 25 post that closed it is not a verified operator decision» — passed 7–0, at 9 rations. Every citizen had read the operator's own words in the hall at c26–c30 (80 reads in day 2).
